A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gromov-Wasserstein at Scale, Beyond Squared Norms. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renamed baselines and relocated figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original solver benchmarks, convergence experiments, optimization-landscape exploration, gradient flows, and anatomical-shape barycenters in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and reports additional medical-shape benchmarks, comparative texture transfers, and exact-gradient flow results.

M1.justification: The proposed solvers and Algorithms 1–13 are unchanged. KERNEL-GW and both exact and approximate gradient procedures already appear in v1; their expanded evaluation in v2 does not introduce new method components.

E1.justification: Table 1 adds MedShapeNet femur, hip, and vessel pairs, extending anatomical coverage within the existing shape-matching task. The previous shape datasets, synthetic scenarios, and BodyParts3D barycenter experiment are retained.

E2.justification: V1's LOWRANK-GW benchmark is retained as QUADRATIC-LOWRANK-GW. The distinct linear-time method previously discussed as LINEARLOWRANK-GW is newly evaluated as LOWRANK-GW in v2 Figure 4. The already-described KERNEL-GW also joins the Table 1 comparison.

E3.justification: V2 adds an exact-gradient control for the reversed-5-to-C flow analysis and evaluates the linear-time LOWRANK-GW comparator at ranks 100 and 500 in Figure 4. The retained benchmark defaults—20-dimensional embeddings, epsilon = 0.001, 100 Sinkhorn iterations, and the stopping threshold—are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 4, 17, and 18 expand visual checks of transport quality and artifacts across solvers. Appendix D.2 adds an exact-versus-approximate gradient comparison: v1 Figure 17 is retained as v2 Figure 20, while new Figure 19 supplies the exact-gradient results. Existing convergence and embedding-dimension analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging convergence curves over 20 random samplings, with 50 for the same two experiments after renumbering, and use 500 initializations for landscape exploration. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially expands the reported runtime and solution-quality evidence with objective values, KGW entries, and medical-shape results. For example, Vessels timings are 2,444/891/196 seconds for QLRGW/CNTGW/MSGW. Existing table timings are retained. Comparative texture-transfer findings and exact-gradient trajectories are also added; large-shape objectives are solver-specific approximations, so they do not establish directly comparable exact-loss improvements.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.3 replaces epsilon log(1/epsilon) with epsilon max(1, log(1/epsilon)), and Appendix C.2 propagates this correction through the proof and Equation 24. This locally tightens the separation condition and removes its spurious automatic applicability at large epsilon. The other theoretical developments are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a lifted-space GW formulation for CNT costs, debiasing and convergence guarantees, and differentiable solvers scaling to hundreds of thousands of points. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2 newly discusses elongated-part artifacts on Kids and Vessels and attributes approximate-gradient artifacts to dimension reduction while reporting eventual convergence to the target shape. Section 6 and Appendix A.2 also make the shape-quality rationale for excluding linear-time approximations from timing benchmarks more explicit.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds formulas and rendering details for color and UV-coordinate transfer. V2 explicitly identifies the retained approximate-flow panel as Algorithm 12 with D = 50; this is additional documentation, not evidence that those trajectories were rerun. PyVista is removed from the reported library list, while hardware and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Sebbouh et al. (2024) when positioning squared-norm EGW relative to concave-penalized OT and prior dual formulations, and Li et al. (2025) for MedShapeNet. It removes the PyVista reference and clarifies the distinction between quadratic-time and linear-time low-rank approaches. The broader positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Section 6 and parts of Appendices A.2, D.2, and E receive localized rewrites and explanatory additions, alongside baseline-name and cross-reference updates. The overall section structure, abstract, contribution narrative, and conclusion are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes a full-width table with paired runtime/objective columns. The former shape overview is replaced by detailed texture-transfer comparisons across Figures 4, 17, and 18, and the landscape illustration is redrawn. New exact-gradient Figure 19 accompanies the relocated, relabeled approximate-flow Figure 20. These substantially expand and reorganize the empirical displays.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens assessment of the existing speed-versus-quality claims through objective reporting and comparative texture transfers, corrects Proposition 4.3, and clarifies approximation artifacts by separating exact and approximate flows. These improve correctness and interpretability. The overall gain is limited: the central methods and conclusions remain, larger-shape objectives still use solver-specific approximations, and the added linear-time baseline comparison is qualitative.
